summary: Steel lookout atop Tobacco Row Mountain, Amherst County, VA; the summit is now a commercial microwave site and the old cab was built into a Long Lines tower.

access.note: Commercial communications site owned by American Tower Corporation; no public visit route found.

evidence.supports: Steel tower on Tobacco Row Mountain, now surrounded by a microwave structure owned by American Tower Corporation; also used for the absence of a build date in the register entry
evidence.quote: This steel tower atop Tobacco Row Mountain is now surrounded by a microwave communications structure owned by American Tower Corporation.

evidence.supports: Long Lines tower stands on the fire tower site; the original observers cabin now holds antennas
evidence.quote: The longlines tower sits on the site of a Fire Tower, which remaining portions of have been integrated into the longlines tower, the most notable point being the original observers cabin at the top, which now houses additional antennae.

evidence.supports: Virginia list marks the tower as standing under NHLR US 1274
evidence.quote: Tobacco Row Amherst 37.56552 -79.19042 Tower Standing NHLR US 1274, VA 40

notes_for_editor: Two searches and about six page reads turned up no build date, designer, staffing record or fire history. The Long Lines page is a hobbyist site, so treat its wording as a lead. The Amherst County memo at https://www.countyofamherst.com/egov/documents/1238777346_488494.pdf appeared in search as a memo about American Tower's use of the 'Old Fire Tower' and repairs to its wooden enclosure. fetch_text found no text layer in it, so it needs a manual read; it may hold the build date and ownership of the cab. The Amherst County survey PDF (DHR, 2009-10) has no mention of a fire tower. Facebook group posts say the tower is no longer used for fire lookout; they are not cited. The brief's access 'unknown' is recorded here as restricted, based on the register's description of a commercial communications site; please confirm.
